name: Kairiru
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 further work by the same author (or citing it for stress) agrees.

new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Primarily stress falls upon the last syllable.
new_statements.citation: Wivell, Richard. n.d. Kairiru Organised Phonology Data. SIL PNG, 4 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives 42459.
new_statements.locator: p. 3, section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' (the one-line section between the vowel-sequence chart and 'Syllable Patterns')
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: the PDF's metadata: 4 pp., 'Kairiru (Tau) OPD, Printed: August 24, 2004'). extracted text gives, between the vowel-sequence chart and 'Syllable Patterns', exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' / 'Primarily stress falls upon the last syllable.' A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole text for stress|tone|length|accent|suprasegmental hits only these two lines (530-531), so the section is the single sentence the compiler describes; the syllable-pattern list that follows carries no stress marks. Reading fixed: final syllable is right and the relation to the catalog alternating stress from the right is 'agrees' on primary placement (final). The OPD is silent on secondary str…
new_statements.relation_note: Catalog alternating stress from the right (an earlier compilation-2026-08-31) = final primary stress with alternating secondaries leftward. The OPD's 'stress falls upon the last syllable' matches the primary-stress placement exactly; it is silent on secondary stress, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the alternating pattern, which the 1981 thesis (same author, held by the project) does confirm.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is on the last syllable of the word. The OPD gives only this one sentence; it does not mention weight, tone, or length effects, and the syllable-pattern list that follows carries no stress marks.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the OPD. (Context, not from this work: Wivell's 1981 MA thesis 'Kairiru Grammar', already held by the project in the same folder, sec. 2.2.1.1 p. 27, reads 'Primary stress falls upon the ultima, secondary stress on the antipenultima and so on', i.e. alternating secondaries leftward from the final syllable, and sec. 2.2.1.2 pp. 27-28 says that within a complex vowel nucleus stress falls on the first vowel of the sequence.)
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the hedge 'Primarily' is the only qualification and no exceptions are listed.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD is headed 'Kairiru (Tau) Language [KXA]', Wewak, East Sepik Province, population 3500 (1977), villages on Kairiru, Karesau, Yuo and Mushu islands plus Wom and Meni Wom; it treats Kairiru as one language and names no dialect. ISO kxa = Glottolog kair1263. The 1981 thesis that it cites in its bibliography is the fuller description of the same variety.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, alternating stress from the right = primary on ultima, secondary on antepenult, alternating leftward) rests on the only reference grammar of the language, Wivell 1981 (MA thesis, 231 pp), whose stress section I opened at p. 27 / sec. 2.2.1.1: the quotation is verbatim (modulo the scanned artefact 'antipenultirna' for 'antipenultima'), and the accompanying schema (((S5) S4) S̀3) S2 Ś1 and transcribed 2-5 syllable examples match the rule string exactly. A second source by the same author, the SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (downloaded now from the Internet Archive), independently states 'Primarily stress falls upon the last syllable.' Glottolog's full 10-item bibliography, Crossref and Semantic Scholar show no later phonology, prosody or instrumental work, and the Ross 2002 sketch is derivative of Wivell. So the record is well-sourced; the only defects are bookkeeping: grade field empty
